subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - Skyline Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - Skyline Health

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and the agreed next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- Bursty inference loads during nightly batch runs and weekday peak hours causing token queueing and latency spikes.
- Regulatory requirement to isolate PHI workloads from other tenants (logical isolation + audit trails).
- Need predictable monthly budgeting for inference costs; current pay-as-you-go with wide variance is a blocker.

Goals we discussed:
- Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) to ensure predictable latency and throughput for patient-facing features.
- VPC/private deployment option for PHI workloads with HSM/KMS integration and comprehensive audit logs.
- SLA target of 99.9% availability for critical routes and p95 latency under 300ms for short inferences.

Proposed high-level dedicated capacity plan (next steps we agreed):
1) Redwood provides a sizing estimate based on your current QPS and 95th percentile token rates — see attached skyline-usage-metrics-q2.csv.
2) Pilot: 2 reserved GPU nodes (NVIDIA A10-equivalent) for 30 days to validate latency/SLOs and autoscale/burst behavior.
3) Security: initiate Private deployment intake (network, KMS, audit requirements) and start SOC2 evidence exchange.
4) Commercials: we will draft a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an initial reserved-capacity quote for review.

Action items / owners:
- Ben: send draft MAP and the sizing assumptions (ETA today) — attached redwood-map-draft.pdf
- Dana: confirm procurement timeline and whether Skyline needs an SOW or PO (by Fri 6/25)
- Marissa/Vivek: join pilot kickoff to validate telemetry, tracing, and audit log collection (TBD)

If this looks right, I’ll loop in our contracts and customer success teams and kick off the MAP.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192

Ben,

Appreciate the clear recap — this aligns with what we discussed.

A couple of clarifications:
- Procurement: we generally require a standard PO and an executed Master Services Agreement. I'll confirm which templates we need by end of day Thursday.
- Pilot scope: can the pilot include a simple canary route for PHI (anonymized) to validate the isolation? Our security team prefers to see the private deployment workflow before we sign off.

I'll also share the internal forecast for Q3 token volumes by tomorrow afternoon so you can refine sizing.

Thanks,
Dana

Thanks — appreciate the procurement note. Attaching the MAP draft and a short FAQ for the pilot. For the PHI canary route we can do one of the following:

- Option A (recommended): Route anonymized patient data through the dedicated cluster in your VPC with strict network rules and KMS-managed keys; we will enable audit logs and a short-lived token exchange for test runs.
- Option B: Synthesize payloads that mirror production distributions for latency/throughput validation (no PHI leaves your environment).

Either approach works; Marissa and Vivek will align on telemetry requirements. We’ll prepare the reserved-capacity quote with 2 GPUs for the 30-day pilot and an optional burst pool.
